what_was_done: Only the ImportError case is fixed. loader.loadTestsFromName catches ImportError alone, so a source-tree test module that fails at import with any other exception still crashes the runner with a traceback and writes no build/junit.xml. Probed on the current runner: tally/test_syn.py holding 'def test_x(:' (SyntaxError) and tally/test_ne.py holding a bare undefined name (NameError) each gave exit 1 and no report. Through the real red gate (gate_project.make_project, story commit adding tally/test_broken.py) both gave the failure 'the test command wrote no JUnit report at build/junit.xml', which is the symptom the finding names. Discovery over tests/ turns the same SyntaxError into an ImportError case, so the two trees still behave differently. The runner's module and build_suite docstrings, the sample README sentence and rewrite/spec/packaging/sample-project.md all claim that an import-broken test module never costs the report; that is false for these cases. The two new tests (test_import_broken_source_module_still_writes_the_report, test_red_survives_an_import_broken_source_module) do fail when the old loadTestsFromModule call is restored, but they only cover ModuleNotFoundError. To finish: in build_suite, wrap the source-tree load in try/except Exception. On failure, add one case named after the module (for example a _FunctionCase) that raises ImportError carrying traceback.format_exc(), so the report keeps type=ImportError as discovery gives. Add a runner-level test and a red-gate test using a syntax-broken tally/test_*.py and one raising NameError at import.

The behaviour is right, but one numbered part of the fix has no test: collecting module-level test_ functions from the source-tree test files (the suite.addTests(_function_cases_of(name)) line in build_suite's */test_*.py loop). In a scratch copy with only that line removed, all 92 gate-unit tests passed, test_sample_runner.py included, while a failing 'def test_ac1_src_red()' in tally/test_fn.py silently left the report and the runner exited 0. On the unmutated runner the same function is reported as a failure, classname tally.test_fn, file tally/test_fn.py. The tests/ half, the parameter rule, the red-gate count and the README sentence are all in place, and each fails when the tests/ collection is removed. To finish: add a runner-level test to test_sample_runner.py that writes tally/test_fn.py with a failing module-level test_ac1_* function and asserts the report case tally.test_fn::<name> is a failure with file_attr tally/test_fn.py and criteria AC-1.
